slides.big: Does the next video really matter?
Researchers gave 24 families a video app for three weeks and changed one thing: what happened when the playlist ended.
When extra videos played by themselves, children watched for longer.
slides.body: Fewer moved on to their next plan. More parents stepped in.

slides.big: How a video ends can change what a child does next.
It's one small study, with young children in the US.
slides.body: It says nothing about older children, or about harm.

slides.kicker: Why it matters to a parent
slides.big: The ending is something you can choose.
A playlist you see first, sized to the age.
slides.note: Hiniker, Heung, Hong and Kientz, CHI 2018. Reference in the comments.
